author: leet-c1
body:
Three guards had holes. Two are proven to have let real regressions through.

## The args/`Use` guard was silently ignoring a shipped command

`parseUsePositionals` only recognized `[<name>]` — square brackets with inner
angle brackets. `cmd/docs_guide.go` declares `Use: "guide [name]"`, the ordinary
Unix convention, which the parser matched not at all — so it treated the command
as documenting **zero** positionals, a near-vacuous bar.

Proven on pristine code: delete `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` from that command
and the guard still passed, while the real binary broke —
`c1i docs guide register-mcp-server` failed with `unknown command`.

Fixed two ways: recognize the bare `[name]` form, **and hard-fail on any bracket
notation none of the known shapes matches**, naming the leftover text. The second
half is the point — it stops the next unrecognized notation being a silent hole
rather than a loud failure.

## That same guard's coverage depended on test order — worse than first measured

The audit found 84 commands checked in isolation versus 89 in a full package run.
Under `-shuffle` it turned out to be a **third** value: **108**.

Two independent causes. Cobra adds `help`/`completion` lazily, only once some other
test calls `Execute`. And `attachSubcommandGuards` — called by five other tests on
the same shared `rootCmd` — installs a synthetic `RunE` on every group command,
flipping `Runnable()` true for 24 of them. So the guard's real subject count was
never pinned down.

Now deterministic at **108**, verified across an isolated run, a full-package run,
seven explicit `-shuffle` seeds, and three random ones. Cobra's lazily-created
commands are excluded deliberately, because production calls
`attachSubcommandGuards` before `ExecuteC` ever creates them — so the guard never
sees them there either.

## The exit-code taxonomy guard only checked one direction

It asserted every `exit*` constant appears in each of the four documents. It never
checked the reverse, so a fabricated row survived indefinitely. Proven: injecting
`| 99 | stale, fabricated row |` into README's table passed with zero errors.

Now both directions. The fabricated row fails with
`documents exit code 99, but no exitXxx constant in cmd/*.go declares it`.

Two known limits deliberately left as documented limits rather than papered over:
the type-assertion-versus-`errors.As` blind spot (already disclosed in the file's
own comment) and `extractTableBlock`'s lookahead.

## Commit order

Committed determinism-first (2→1→3), because fixing the parser blind spot alone
trips on cobra's own `help` command in a full-package run — the determinism fix
has to land first for every commit in the history to be independently green.
Each of the three was verified independently buildable and green.

author: startupbros
body:
## Summary

PR #238 added a declared parity floor in `packages/http-api/src/services/cache-parity-expectations.ts` (79% weighted cache-read / 10% zero-hit), set from the same measurement it's meant to police. Measured live in production, the authoritative 7-day Codex cohort now sits at 79.1% weighted / 9.1% zero-hit — only **0.1 percentage points** of headroom on the weighted floor.

This is a design defect: the floor exists to catch a genuine regression in the cache-reuse gain the campaign won, but at 0.1pp of margin it will instead fire on ordinary week-to-week drift. An alarm that fires on noise gets ignored, which defeats its purpose.

## Fix

Retune the floor to `weightedCacheReadPercent: 75`, `zeroHitRatePercent: 12`, with a comment recording the three reference points:

- **Pre-campaign baseline** (issue #174): 43.6% weighted, 32.7% zero-hit.
- **Currently achieved and measured**: 79.1% weighted / 9.1% zero-hit (authoritative 7-day window), 81.2% weighted / 7.2% zero-hit (24-hour window).
- **New floor (75 / 12)**: ~4pp below the achieved weighted level and ~3pp above the achieved zero-hit level — real drift margin, while still enormously far from the pre-campaign state, so a breach still means the gain was actually lost, not that the metric wiggled.

Also updated the matching floor numbers in `docs/configuration.md` for consistency, and extended `cache-parity-expectations.test.ts` with explicit boundary tests (exactly-at-floor holds; just-below-weighted and just-above-zero-hit both breach).

Refs #174, #233. Not merging — for review.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test packages/http-api/src/services/__tests__/cache-parity-expectations.test.ts packages/http-api/src/services/__tests__/cache-parity.test.ts` — 18 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bun run lint` — same 8 pre-existing warnings unrelated to this change (none in touched files); re-ran once, stable
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun run format` — no fixes applied

author: bragamask
body:
## Contexto

Esta branch conclui a remediação de segurança iniciada anteriormente e corrige uma
regressão crítica introduzida por ela.

Durante a auditoria foi constatado, em execução no navegador, que a aplicação
estava **inoperante**: o `credentials: "include"` adicionado na etapa anterior é
incompatível com o `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` que a API responde, e o
navegador bloqueava toda requisição.

```
Access to fetch ... has been blocked by CORS policy: The value of the
'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header in the response must not be the
wildcard '*' when the request's credentials mode is 'include'.
```

A especificação OpenAPI real da API (`/api/v1/docs/openapi.v3.json`) foi usada
como fonte de verdade e contradiz o contrato de cookie assumido antes.

## Principais mudanças

### Autenticação

- Modo de autenticação controlado por `VITE_AUTH_MODE` (`bearer` por padrão).
  O modo `cookie` fica pronto, mas desativado até o backend suportá-lo.
- Sessão obtida de `GET /autenticacao/quem-sou-eu`, tratando `usuario: null`
  com HTTP 200 como anônimo. A chamada ocorre uma única vez na inicialização.
- **Papel derivado de dados explícitos do servidor** (`perfisAtivos[].cargo` e
  `usuario.isSuperUser`), substituindo as heurísticas que inspecionavam o texto
  do JWT e contavam dígitos da matrícula.
- **Correção de escalonamento de privilégio**: a função anterior retornava
  `"admin"` como fallback. Agora papel desconhecido ou vazio **nega acesso**.
- Token mantido apenas em memória; nada em `localStorage` ou `sessionStorage`.
- `jwt-decode` removido: o JWT deixou de ser fonte de verdade no cliente.

### Tratamento de erros

- Erros classificados em rede, timeout, 401, 403, 404 e 5xx, com mensagens
  seguras que não repassam detalhes internos do backend.
- Timeout de 15s via `AbortController`: sem isso, uma requisição pendurada
  mantinha a interface em carregamento indefinido.
- Removido o redirecionamento direto por `window.location`, que podia gerar
  laço de navegação. O encerramento de sessão é notificado ao contexto e a
  navegação fica a cargo do roteador.
- `alert()` substituído por mensagens na interface com `role="alert"`.

### Qualidade

- `npm run lint` passa com exit 0. Os 5 erros e os 4 avisos de
  `security/detect-object-injection` foram resolvidos por refatoração,
  **sem nenhum `eslint-disable`**.
- Corrigido bug de mutação de estado em `CadastroVagaForm`: `[...horarios]` é
  cópia rasa e a atribuição aninhada mutava o objeto original.
- Telas ainda sem endpoint (`AvaliarEmpresa`, `FolhaDePontos`) deixaram de
  afirmar sucesso e passaram a sinalizar que estão em desenvolvimento.

### Testes e CI

- Vitest e Testing Library, com 37 testes cobrindo sessão anônima, reload,
  login, logout, 401, timeout, ausência de token persistido e negação de
  acesso administrativo sem papel explícito.
- Workflow de CI executando lint, testes, build, auditoria de dependências e
  varredura de segredos com falha obrigatória.

### Documentação

- `SECURITY.md` reescrito: substitui o template genérico do GitHub, que trazia
  versões fictícias, por política real com canal de reporte e procedimento para
  credencial exposta.
- `ISSUE_BACKEND_AUTH_COOKIE.md` corrigido conforme a OpenAPI. A versão anterior
  citava `/autenticacao/sessao`, que não existe.

## Validações executadas

| Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | 0 vulnerabilidades |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | 37 testes, 4 arquivos |
| `npm run build` | sucesso |
| `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` | 0 vulnerabilidades |
| `gitleaks dir` / `gitleaks detect` | nenhum vazamento |

Verificado também no navegador: `/empresas` voltou a responder 200 e rotas
protegidas redirecionam corretamente para `/login`.

## Limitação conhecida

No modo `bearer`, **a sessão é perdida ao recarregar a página**, pois nada é
persistido no navegador. Isso é intencional e só se resolve com cookie
`httpOnly` emitido pelo backend.

## Pendências de backend e infraestrutura

| Item | Situação |
|---|---|
| CORS com origem explícita e `Allow-Credentials` | Pré-requisito para o modo cookie |
| Cookie `httpOnly` + `csrf_token` | Não existe |
| `POST /autenticacao/logout` | Não existe; logout é apenas local |
| Enum oficial de `cargo` | Não documentado; cargos desconhecidos ficam sem acesso |
| CSP `frame-ancestors` por header HTTP | Não há arquivo de deploy no repositório |

> **A rotação das credenciais expostas permanece pendente e é a ação mais
> urgente.** O repositório é público, então a limpeza de histórico já realizada
> não desfaz a exposição.

author: ahmedbahahalil
body:
The companion to [3pl-management#459](https://github.com/ahmedbahahalil/3pl-management/pull/459), which installed quality gates across the backend and Flutter app. The marketing site lives in this repo, so its share of that work lands here.

`npx eslint .` is **clean**.

## What's here

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — written rules Claude Code loads automatically, matching the sibling files in the product repo.
- **`eslint.config.mjs`** — flat config for the site's browser JavaScript.
- **`package.json`** — pins the lint toolchain only. No runtime dependencies, no build step; the site is still plain HTML, CSS and script tags.
- One code change: a comment inside a deliberately empty `catch`.

## What was dropped, deliberately

The generic pack assumed a Next.js app. This site isn't one, so two of its three tools were removed rather than carried over:

- **`eslint-plugin-boundaries`** enforces layering between import paths.
- **`knip`** traces unused exports through an import graph.

Neither an import graph nor layers exist on a static site loaded via script tags. Both would have run green while checking nothing, which is worse than not running them, because it looks like coverage.

## Generated bundles excluded

`walkthroughs/support.js` and `fariiq_walkthroughs_site/support.js` carry a `GENERATED from dc-runtime/src/*.ts — do not edit` header. They were **132 of the initial 147 errors**. Linting a build artifact produces findings nobody can act on.

## The one code change

`js/translations.js` had an empty `catch` around `localStorage.setItem`. That was intentional — localStorage throws in private mode and when cookies are blocked, and the language switch should still work for the current page load even if the choice can't persist. Nothing said so, so it read like a swallowed error. Stating the intent also satisfies `no-empty`, which ignores blocks containing a comment.

## Noted, not fixed

`walkthroughs/` and `fariiq_walkthroughs_site/` overlap, and their `support.js` files are byte-identical. Collapsing them is a genuine cleanup but belongs in its own PR, so `CLAUDE.md` records the trap instead: editing one and forgetting the other is easy to do.

## No CI

This repo has no workflows, and I didn't add one, since that's a bigger call than installing a lint config. The gate runs locally with `npx eslint .`. Happy to add a workflow if you want it enforced on PRs.

author: leet-c1
body:
`c1i apps list --fields bogus_field` wrote **46 lines of `{}` to stdout**, then
exited 2. The exit code was right; stdout lied first. Anything reading stdout
without checking `$?` — the most common pipeline mistake, and this CLI exists for
`jq` pipelines — saw 46 syntactically valid, semantically empty objects.

Rows whose projection is empty are now skipped. If nothing matches anywhere,
nothing is printed and the existing zero-match check still exits 2, so stdout
never lies. No buffering, so no memory or latency cost on a 35,000-row list.

Verified: `--fields totally_bogus` on `main` prints 46 lines and exits 2; on this
branch it prints **0** lines and exits 2.

## A second defect this fix created, and fixed

Skipping rows decouples "rows processed" from "rows written" — and `--limit` was
comparing against a locally incremented counter that assumed they were the same.
So a sparse `--fields` plus `--limit` could stop pagination early, under-delivering
rows; in `api --paginate` it could even produce a spurious zero-match exit 2
because the real match sat on a page never fetched.

Fixed by adding `emitter.Written()` — incremented only when a line is actually
written — and driving `limitReached`/`effectivePageSize` from that instead of the
parallel tally. This is the same trap that bit `functions usage`, where a shared
helper assumed fetched-equals-emitted and stopped holding once a command filtered
client-side.

Two new tests, both proven red against the pre-fix code.

**On the 4-versus-5 live case:** I initially could not reproduce it — my sample
found `outcome` present on 35 of the first 40 tasks, so the limit was satisfied
before sparsity mattered. Review reproduced it and explained the gap: the sparsity
comes from a small cluster of no-outcome tasks near the front of a live, actively
changing tenant, so it is position- and timing-dependent. On `main` the command
prints 5 lines of which only 4 are real (one is a literal `{}`) and stops after a
single HTTP request, leaving the genuine fifth match unfetched on page 2; on this
branch it returns 5 real matches across 2 requests. The claim is accurate.

author: fheikens
body:
Bumps the Control Plane Catalog template for the public pgAgroal container to the 1.4.5 release and surfaces the frontend TLS that 1.4.5 added.

## What changed

- **Image pin -> 1.4.5.** The reviewed production image is pinned to the `pgagroal:1.4.5` multi-arch index (`sha256:36017745ebd98816c9adac5868965f32b06f72a4049b5fb107cd5bef629fbfcb`, verified against ghcr). `image.repository`/`image.digest` remain immutable and fail-fast if changed.
- **Frontend TLS (client -> pooler), off by default.** New `tls.{enabled,cert,key,mutualTLS,caCert}` values. When enabled, the PEM cert/key (and CA for mutual TLS) are stored as Control Plane **opaque** secrets, revealed only to the pgAgroal identity via the bundled policy, and mounted read-only; the entrypoint installs the key at `0600`. `mutualTLS` enables `verify-ca` client-certificate checking — the pgagroal 2.1.0 pooler has no `tls_cert_auth_mode` key, so `verify-full` is not offered. Backend TLS remains out of scope.
- **Fail-fast validation** for the new inputs (boolean switches; cert+key required when enabled; `mutualTLS` requires `enabled` + `caCert`).
- **Docs:** README + LISTING replace the old "TLS not configurable" limitation with frontend-TLS instructions and updated positioning.
- **Tests:** new `PGA-R012` acceptance cases — off-by-default, opt-in render (env + opaque secrets + reveal + mounts), mutual TLS, and the fail-fast negatives.

## Validation

- `helm lint` clean; `helm template` renders with defaults (upstream `validate-charts.yml` parity) and for TLS-on / mutual-TLS.
- Full acceptance suite (`tests/render-acceptance.sh`) passes, including all `PGA-R012` cases.
- Pinned digest confirmed against the published `ghcr.io/elevarq/pgagroal:1.4.5` index.

body:
The state-model half of **P2/M3**. Replaces the single `SESSION: RwLock<Session>` with a registry keyed by `SteerKey`, where `SteerKey::default()` is the **unscoped** session every existing un-keyed function operates on.

**All 27 pre-existing tests pass unchanged**, because nothing about today's callers moved. Independent of PRs #266 and #268 — branches off `master`.

## API

Un-keyed functions delegate to the default key; `_for` variants take one:
`begin_apply_for`, `begin_capture_for`, `commit_capture_for`, `finish_capture_for`, `clear_for`, `is_active_for`, `maybe_steer_block_for`, `maybe_steer_block_batched_for`. Plus `clear_all` for model load/unload — a spec captured against one model must not survive into the next.

## Two decisions about the safe direction of error

**`ACTIVE` stays one bool** meaning "any session is active". The hot path keeps paying exactly one relaxed load regardless of how many streams carry specs; a stream with no spec pays a map lookup only when someone else is steering. The gate can't be per-key without the hot path knowing the key *before* it checks the gate.

**`EPOCH` stays one counter** across all keys. A per-key epoch is the eventual optimisation, but a shared counter errs the right way: bumping it for another stream's change makes this stream's apply cache refresh when it needn't (a wasted upload), whereas a per-key counter that *missed* a bump would reuse another stream's uploaded directions — silently steering with the wrong vector. Over-invalidate until `APPLY_CACHE` is keyed too.

## Two correctness details

- `with_session` drops its write guard before `refresh_active_gate` takes a **read** lock on the same map. Re-entering would deadlock the thread.
- The gate is recomputed from the **whole map**, not from the mutated entry, so one stream going inactive cannot clear it while another is still steering.

## Tests

Four new (31 total): keyed sessions don't alias and clearing one doesn't disarm another; the unscoped session is exactly the default key; keyed capture accumulates independently; `clear_all` drops everything.

Verified they have teeth — making `with_session` ignore the key fails `keyed_capture_accumulates_independently`. Worth noting the falsification hit only that test: `set_session_for` writes the map directly while capture goes through `with_session`, so the two tests cover different accessors rather than duplicating.

## Serving numerics unchanged

This is an explicit stop-line in the prerequisite plan, so it's measured rather than argued: `gpu_validate` **ALL PASS**, 18 cases, with error figures **identical** to the pre-change run (sync-stress `6.11e-7`, capture→derive `2.38e-7`).

`no-gpu-ci` exit 0; `hipfire-steer` rustfmt-clean.

## What's left for M3's exit

The hook still needs the stream's key threaded to it from the forward, and the daemon steer handler needs to accept `session_id` and route to `begin_apply_for`. Both are now mechanical; this PR removes the reason they couldn't be done.

author: jcalderabarboza-star
body:
Off `main` @ `4f14d80`. Floor **3275/238 → 3321/241**. All four gates green.

## Item 6 — the dead end, and why the ruling's reason was the wrong half

§67 left `Draft` without an exit, stating on the surface that a submit affordance would be *"a REQUESTER act for a document this platform does not originate… a second creation path beside the ratified C7 seam."*

**`t_pr_submit` is not creation.** It acts on a document `t_pr_create` has already minted (C7 :131 → Draft; C7 :132 → Pending Approval), so it adds no producer at all and the C7 argument never applied. C7 is untouched; option (a) refused.

The consequence that had shipped: **the approval surface could empty a queue and nothing could fill it.** Every approval it ever performed was against `pr-004`, a seeded fixture. Derived — `t_pr_submit` and `t_pr_revise` both had **zero call sites** (only i18n purpose keys and `annotations.ts` catalogue rows, which describe verbs rather than call them).

And it is the verb that makes the segregation **real rather than notional**: `pr:submit` ∈ `requisitioner`, `pr:approve` ∈ `procurement`, disjoint since §64 — but until something dispatched the requester side, that disjointness was a property of the bundles no test and no surface ever exercised. The new spec walks create → submit → reject → revise → submit → approve, and **neither narrow seat can complete it alone.**

## 1 · `revisionNote` — a full enforcement chain terminating in nothing

Required by `t_pr_revise` since PF-1a, refused with `MISSING_FIELDS`, then dropped before the document was written. Whole-tree derivation before building: the identifier appeared only in specs, the flow's `requiredFields`, and two `findings.md` lines — **no DTO field, no store write, no reader.**

Repaired with the `rejectionReason` template: optional DTO field · required on the verb · `PR_REVISION_NOTE_AUTHORED` (non-blank; `isEmpty('   ')` is FALSE) · **persisted** · read back beside the rejection reason. Both survive the edges: one says why it came back, the other what was done about it.

## 2 · Attribution — two premises inverted, one against the contract

⚠️ **`actor: 'buyer:all'` is not a stale string.** It is `actorKey(scope)`, derived at emit time, and **C10 §6.4 explicitly rules that it stays**: *"the persona actor is a true fact about the scope… collapsing them is `ENF-EVENT-ACTOR-IS-A-PERSONA-01` with extra steps."* Executed as written, this batch would have committed the named anti-pattern. (Also: `grantedBy` is on the unmerged #251, so the pattern ships **once** on main, not twice.)

The conclusion was right anyway — the ledger could not name a human. But **the obvious build was the one C10 forbids**: a required `approvedBy` payload field mirroring `setBy` is *attribution by assertion* (§6.2), permitted there only because nothing can construct a `RESOLVED` actor yet. Copying it would have doubled the seam this batch exists to close.

- The actor comes from the **session** — `applyTransition` gained a 4th parameter, `scope`; every existing target ignores it.
- `PR_APPROVAL_ATTRIBUTED` **refuses a payload-supplied `approvedBy` by name** — §6.2's second half, **first implementation in the tree**. Refused **by key, not by value-shape**: refusing only a well-formed actor lets a malformed one through to be dropped silently.
- `TransitionEvent.attribution` (§6.4), set **only on `trigger: 'user'`** — a cascade re-dispatches under the same scope, and stamping machine acts `UNATTRIBUTED` floods the vocabulary whose count is the only pressure to fix one. Free now; DR-10 has no retrofit.

## 3 · `approver` — neither "written" nor "not rendered"

Both readings assume it is an approver. Derived: `pr-004` is **Pending Approval** carrying `'Section Head'`; `pr-005` is **Draft** carrying `'—'`; values are role bands tracking `estimatedValue`; no verb ever wrote one. **A field populated before the act it names cannot be a record of that act.** It is the routing destination, misnamed — §67's label defect one layer down, in a DTO.

`approver` → `approvalLevel`, labelled *"Routes to"*. The actor is now `approvedBy`, written by the verb and **absent until somebody approves.**

## Also found

- **The stored-field gate went red unprompted** and was right: `ActorAttribution.person`'s exemption said *"nothing reads one"*, which stopped being true. Row deleted.
- **A fifth false affordance, in the toast:** `'Routed to Section Head for approval.'` fired by `t_pr_create`, which mints a Draft. §67 fixed the button and walked past the toast it fires. The class now has four homes — handler · shape · label · **confirmation**.

## Solid action-blue, retired portal-wide (operator ruling, mid-batch)

This **reverses** DP2-BUTTON-01, under which §67 deliberately made *Confirm rejection* solid. CLAUDE.md is amended.

⚠️ **`grep 'variant="primary"'` found 14 sites and was wrong four ways:** a **prop** (`BulkActionsBar.primary.solid`), a **model flag** (`invoiceActionModel.solid` — which *also drove a confirmation step*, so deleting it with the styling would have deleted behaviour; renamed `reservedCommit`), **two typed helpers** returning `'primary' | 'outline'`, and **`Button`'s own default**, which made solid the shape of forgetting to choose.

**The last two were found by the type**, after removing `'primary'` from the `Variant` union — not by any scan. The rule is now a `tsc` failure; the gate covers what a type cannot.

The gate falsely accused two files on its first runs, both times for a comment **explaining the rule** — a rule stated in the file it governs is always readable as a violation of itself. `withoutProse` fixes it.

## Verification

- **7 mutation probes**, green baseline confirmed first, each killing a **named** test (4/3/5/1/3/1/1). Zero residue.
- **Browser QA** on the built bundle, cache-busted, **both locales**: full loop verified in ID and EN; 295 buttons across 7 surfaces, **zero solid** — and a synthetic `#0070F2` button injected into the same scan **was** caught, because zero is the answer that requires checking the instrument.

## Still open

`t_pr_reject` records no decider on the document (ruling named approve; pinned by test) · `setBy` is still attribution-by-assertion · items 4/5/7 untouched by ruling · `disputeReason` remains the last chain-terminating-in-nothing.

## 概述

支持对上游 opencode 运行时进行 Basic 鉴权、单点声明支持的上游版本线，并新增真实集成冒烟测试。由 #495 跟踪。

## 改动内容

1. **上游鉴权支持**
   - 新增设置 `OPENCODE_AUTH_USERNAME`（默认 `opencode`）与 `OPENCODE_AUTH_PASSWORD`（默认未设置）。
   - 配置密码后，所有上游调用（含 SSE `/event` 流）携带 `Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)>`，与上游 `opencode serve` 的 `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` / `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` 契约对齐；未配置时不发送该头（默认行为不变）。
   - 密码字段设置 `repr=False`，避免意外出现在 `Settings` 的 repr 中。
   - `docs/guide.md` 环境变量清单同步补充说明。

2. **上游版本线单点声明**
   - `docs/compatibility.md` Runtime Support 新增 `OpenCode runtime line: 1.18.x (verified with 1.18.19)`，并注明该处为唯一规范位置，不再于其他文档重复维护。

3. **真实集成冒烟 `scripts/live_opencode_smoke.sh`**
   - 启动真实（密码加固）`opencode serve` + opencode-a2a，验证：上游鉴权强制（无凭据 401）、适配器 `/health`、JSON-RPC 扩展读方法（`opencode.projects.current` / `opencode.sessions.status`）、流式对话端到端（`SendStreamingMessage` → `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`）。
   - 全部运行于 `mktemp -d` 临时根：隔离的 opencode HOME/XDG、临时 workspace、显式临时 SQLite URL、随机端口；`trap` 退出即清理，不触碰任何有效数据目录。
   - 所有就绪/探测请求带 `--max-time`，服务器启动窗口异常时快速失败而非无限挂起；适配器直接使用 `.venv/bin/opencode-a2a` 启动（`$!` 即真实服务进程，清理可靠）。
   - 手动/本地入口，与 `conformance.sh` 同级，**不接入** doctor/CI 默认回归基线（按仓库互操作实验策略）。

## 相关 commits

- `6082774` feat: support authenticated OpenCode upstream and add live integration smoke
- `1e26b2f` fix: harden live smoke robustness and hide upstream password from repr

## 验证

- `./scripts/doctor.sh` 全绿：706 tests passed，coverage 93.01%（门槛 ≥90%），pre-commit / mypy / 构建 / wheel 冒烟均通过。
- `./scripts/live_opencode_smoke.sh` 对安装版 opencode 1.18.19 实测全绿（含密码加固上游下的流式对话）。
- GitHub Actions（Default Toolchain、Runtime Matrix 3.11/3.12）全部通过。

- Closes #495（本 PR 完整实现该 issue 范围）。

author: rizwandar
body:
## Summary

Low-priority backlog item OPS-28. Adds a show/hide (eye) toggle to every password input in the app, using one new shared component instead of the ad hoc per-form implementations that had grown up independently.

## What changed

**New component:** `client/src/components/PasswordInput.jsx` - wraps react-bootstrap's `Form.Control` in an `InputGroup` with a Show/Hide toggle `Button`, managing its own show/hide state internally. Forwards all props (value, onChange, placeholder, autoComplete, isInvalid, onKeyDown, style, size, ref, etc.) straight through to the underlying `Form.Control`, so it is a drop-in swap for `<Form.Control type="password" ... />`.

This reuses the exact InputGroup + outline-secondary Button + "Show"/"Hide" text pattern that already existed independently in a few forms (no icon library is installed in this project, so no eye/eye-slash icon glyph exists; "Show"/"Hide" was the app's own established convention for this exact feature, now consolidated into one place instead of four).

**Every password field updated** (32 `type="password"` occurrences across 10 files, plus 4 fields that already had a hand-rolled show/hide toggle, all consolidated):

- `client/src/pages/LoginPage.jsx` - login password
- `client/src/pages/RegisterPage.jsx` - password, confirm password
- `client/src/pages/ResetPasswordPage.jsx` - new password, confirm new password
- `client/src/pages/OrgAdminInviteCompletePage.jsx` - choose a password
- `client/src/pages/org/OrgTokenPage.jsx` - choose a password
- `client/src/pages/ProfilePage.jsx` - account password change (both render paths), security question current password, security question removal confirm password, vault password change (old/new/confirm), vault reset confirm password, vault recovery setup/disable passwords, destroy/logout/lockout threshold confirm passwords, delete-account password and vault password (17 fields total)
- `client/src/pages/ExportPage.jsx` - vault password for full export (already had a hand-rolled toggle)
- `client/src/pages/sections/DigitalLifePage.jsx` - credential password field (already had a hand-rolled toggle)
- `client/src/components/VaultGate.jsx` - vault setup password + confirm, account password confirm (full reset), vault unlock password (confirm field previously had no toggle at all; setup field already had one)
- `client/src/components/VaultRecoverForm.jsx` - new vault password + confirm
- `client/src/components/ShareSectionTrigger.jsx` - vault password for sharing

No `type="password"` Form.Control and no raw `<input type="password">` remain anywhere in `client/src`.

Confirmed out of scope / not password inputs: `ForgotPasswordPage.jsx` (email only, no password field), `DeleteAccountPage.jsx` (static help text page, no form), `VaultSecurityPanel.jsx` (no password field), `DigitalLifePage.jsx`'s per-item "show" toggle on saved credentials (read-only display of a stored value, not an `<input>`).

## Security note (per task instructions)

Confirmed toggling visibility is purely a client-side rendering change: it only flips the `type` attribute of the underlying `<input>` between `"password"` and `"text"` in the browser. It does not touch how the value is captured, transmitted, stored, or logged - all of that logic lives in each form's own `onChange`/`onSubmit` handlers, which are untouched. No code path was found that special-cases `type="password"` in a way this would break (no `.type` reads and no password-manager-specific handling beyond the browser's own native `type="password"` autofill heuristics, which is expected, standard behavior for this pattern).

**No backend changes needed or made** - this PR touches only `client/src`.

## Verification

- `cd client && npm run lint` - 0 errors, 20 pre-existing warnings (none introduced by this change, none touch the changed files' logic)
- `cd client && npm run build` - succeeds

## Not done (per task instructions)

Not merging this PR, not promoting to `main`, and not running `/security-review` - purely client-side UI convenience feature, no new attack surface.
